buginformation.summary: Workspace plug-in model stores stale bundle description
buginformation.description: Follow up to Bug 417096. When there is a problem with the bundle description we don't add it to the model. However, we also do not clear any existing bundle description, so the previous stale description will be used.In MinimalState.addBundle() line 76, when we catch a exception from creating the bundle description, we should clear the existing bundle description.

buginformation.summary: [patch] Add ability to allow Eclipse debug trace to stdout and stderr
buginformation.description: In the existing eclipse debug trace framework org.eclipse.osgi.service.debug.DebugTrace, the trace output can only have the option to generate to a particular file. In case there are components that are still using stdout and stderr for their trace and have not moved to the new debug trace framework yet, it is difficult to keep the correlation on traces on different components since the trace output will be on different location.This proposed feature is to provide an extra preference settings on the Trace settings GUI to allow the user to have an option to output the trace to the stdout and stderr.

buginformation.summary: ManifestUtils should print Manifest-Version key in the first line of the MANIFEST.MF file
buginformation.description: The ManifestUtils class (from org.eclipse.pde.core 3.10.0 - Eclipse Luna) prints out the contents of the MANIFEST.MF file in a bad format. The Manifest-Version key-value pair should be printed in the first line of the file (instead it is handled only after the distinguished keys have been processed, see writeManifest method lines 249-260). This will cause problems when the manifest merging functionality is invoked from the org.eclipse.emf.codegen.ecore.generator.AbstractGeneratorAdapter class, because it is looking for the Manifest-Version to be the first entry in the file. In the previos version of the org.eclipse.pde.core plugin (version 3.9.0 - Eclipse Kepler) the ManifestUtils class did not exist, instead the PluginConverter class had a writeManifest method which handled the Manifest-Version key properly. Why did the implementation change? According to this site http://www.cis.upenn.edu/~bcpierce/courses/629/jdkdocs/guide/jar/manifest.html this entry should be the first in the file. At the moment this is a blocker issue for https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=419128.

buginformation.summary: Remove Error Log view from default PDE perspective
buginformation.description: In the vogella trainings, a significant amount of participants are usually confused by the presence of the error log. They (newbies) don't understand that the errors are coming from the running IDE and not their RCP app. Thus, I wonder if we give too much attention to the error log or if it is better left hidden to be used by more experienced users.Also showing the error log right from startup might lead users to think Eclipse is not stable.Btw. I do know that the error log supports showing the log of the nested RCP app.

buginformation.summary: Luna should allow to convert 2.0-style plug-in to OSGi bundle with manifest
buginformation.description: I20131112-0800Luna should still allow to convert a 2.0-style plug-in from my workspace to an OSGi bundle with a MANIFEST.MF.2.0-style plug-ins were only seriously deprecated very late in Kepler, but they still worked there. Now, when I start Luna and have an old-style plug-in in my workspace (e.g. org.eclipse.swt.snippets from R4_3_maintenance), Ia) don't get any error in the Problems viewb) get a silent error in the log (the PDE builder should create a problem marker instead of a log entry):!ENTRY org.eclipse.pde.core 4 201 2013-11-18 15:05:39.250!MESSAGE Plug-in at 'C:\e\i\I20131112-0800\a\org.eclipse.swt.snippets' does not have a manifest. The PluginConverter service used to create manifests for old style plug-ins is not available, please install the 'org.eclipse.osgi.compatibility.plugins' compatibility fragment.c) can't convert the bundle to OSGi by clicking the "create an OSGi bundle manifest" link in the manifest editor.It's OK that Luna doesn't support 2.0-style plug-ins any more, but it still has to help the user with the transition. The advice to install the 'org.eclipse.osgi.compatibility.plugins' is bad. Normally, a user should NOT install that bundle, but should just fix the project. The compatibility bundle is not even easily available (bug 412886 comment 15). And I guess once it's installed, the user wouldn't even be forced to fix their bundle -- which is exactly the opposite from what we want to achieve.

buginformation.summary: [patch] [target] TargetContentsGroup does not consider custom location images
buginformation.description: In the TargetContentsGroup one can group the plugins by location. If a custom location type is involved then its icon doesn't show up, which looks odd. The cause is that TargetContentsGroup.createTree() uses a plain StyledBundleLabelProvider. With this code it seems to work for me:fTree.setLabelProvider(new StyledBundleLabelProvider(true, false) { @Override public Image getImage(Object element) { Image image = super.getImage(element); if (image == null element instanceof ITargetLocation) { ILabelProvider provider = (ILabelProvider) Platform.getAdapterManager() .getAdapter(element, ILabelProvider.class); if (provider != null) { image = provider.getImage(element); } } return image; }});

buginformation.summary: Let subclasses of AbstractBundleContainer specify smoother progress monitoring for resolve()
buginformation.description: My subclass of AbstractBundleContainer does all the resolve() work in resolveBundles() and resolveFeatures() just returns the already cached fFeatures.In this scenario it's a little annoying that resolve() allocates one third of the overall work to resolveFeatures() in a hardcoded way.https://git.eclipse.org/r/#/c/21720/ adds override points for subclasses with a work ratio different from 2/1. With the current defaults it should not impact existing subclasses, but maybe some of them could make use of the new methods, too.

buginformation.summary: [patch] ErrorLog view duplicates statuses
buginformation.description: Created attachment 240423Target file to reproduce the problemThe ErrorLog view duplicates the children of MultiStatus entries. This code that has been changed in the context of bug 416507 to LogView.createLogEntry(IStatus) adds new child entries: private LogEntry createLogEntry(IStatus status) { LogEntry entry = new LogEntry(status); // [...] if (status.isMultiStatus()) { IStatus[] children = status.getChildren(); for (int i = 0; i children.length; i++) { LogEntry childEntry = createLogEntry(children[i]); entry.addChild(childEntry); childEntry.setSession(currentSession); } }But child entries for the child statuses have already been added in new LogEntry(status).The problem can be reproduced with the attached test.target file. Just open it in an IDE and "Set as Target Platform". It shouldn't be able to resolve properly and as a result add nested multi statuses. They're displayed incorrectly in the ErrorLog view as you can see in the screenshot that I'll also attach.I've submitted a Gerrit review that also fixes the problem that the implicitely created child entries have no session set:https://git.eclipse.org/r/#/c/22151/

buginformation.summary: TargetLocationContentProvider shouldn't check "instanceof MultiStatus"
buginformation.description: Near the bottom of TargetLocationContentProvider.getChildren() there is this code: } else if (parentElement instanceof MultiStatus) { return ((MultiStatus) parentElement).getChildren(); } else { ... }But the getChildren() methdod is declared in IStatus. The current instanceof check prevents IStatus implementations other than MultiStatus from showing their children. The fix is easy: } else if (parentElement instanceof IStatus) { return ((IStatus) parentElement).getChildren(); } else { ... }I'm going to submit a Gerrit review...

buginformation.summary: Support the root level features attribute installMode="root" in the product configuration editor
buginformation.description: Our solution for the most-wanted Tycho feature (bug 361722) included adding the attribute "installMode" in product/features/feature elements in product configuration files.We are recommending our users to use the PDE Product Configuration editor for product files, so I wondered if it is possible to add some support for our extension of your product file format in the editor. The absolute minimum would already help: just have the editor leave the attribute unchanged when doing other modifications. If you say that this change is acceptable, we'll probably find someone from the Tycho community to contribute a patch.The background of the Tycho feature is the following: Tycho can create installations/distribution archives from product files. Up to recently, these installations only contained one root element, the product, so it was not possible (or only with advanced p2 magic) to create an installation where the installed features can be updated independently of the product. With Tycho 0.20.0, this has become a lot easier - to see how, try out this demo build:1. git clone https://git.eclipse.org/r/tycho/org.eclipse.tycho-demo.git2. git fetch origin refs/changes/59/23059/1 git checkout FETCH_HEAD 3. Follow the instructions here: https://git.eclipse.org/r/#/c/23059/

buginformation.summary: PDE Manifest editor: Missing 2.0 compatibility should be shown as error
buginformation.description: 4.4 RC2.FUP of bug 421979.My test case always imported one of my demo bundles from CVS and then I replaced it with a version that did not have a manifest. Unfortunately, PDE can populate the PDE container during the initial import and then keeps it after replace. However, if one closes and reopens the project, or directly imports a 2.0 style bundle, then the PDE container won't resolve and the project stays full of errors. Hence, we should show an error when the compatibility bundle isn't installed and the message should say "to compile or run".
